PlayLiberty design / screens / playlist detail
Screens

Playlist detail

The screen the product exists for: the only place stored tracks become audible. It composes the playlist header, the track row, the sync summary, the sync error, the empty state and the player bar, and its own work is to arrange them, gate three controls on access, and cover the states a playlist can be in.

Two arrangements, and both are drawn. Web is /playlists/:id at 1056 by 900 and mobile is pushed over the library root at 390 by 844. Every measurement below says which one it came from, and the two are kept in separate sections rather than interleaved frame by frame, because a page showing a desk, a phone, a desk and a phone is read as four screens with two layouts each. The two dialogs this screen hosts and the not-found state are named in the last section with what each of them still needs, rather than left out without a word.

The web arrangement, at 1056 and 900

1056 is the content column the library's own web arrangement is laid out in, and the two are meant to be comparable, so this frame takes its 1px border out of the 1056 rather than out of it. 900 is a viewport height and it is stated because on web the width is not the constraint and the height is, and a frame with no height cannot answer a question about it. The library's own web arrangement has no frame at all, which is why it makes no claim about height.

Two columns. The left carries the playlist: the header's own card at 320px, then one component beneath it. The right carries the tracks, the track row at 712px. The player's bar is docked along the bottom, which is the first screen in the product where the bar is drawn at rest, and the bar's own record scopes its arrival to exactly this: a person who has opened a playlist is somewhere they chose to be, and the bar is persistent once playback exists.

The left column is the header's card arrangement, unmodified, and that is the argument for the whole column. The header has a row arrangement and a card arrangement, and this is the second of them at 320px rather than the 356.4 the library draws it at. There is no third arrangement, and nothing about the component is re-decided here. What the narrower column costs is measured: a 288px cover against the header's own 324.4px, a scrim that is 27.8% of the picture against 24.7% of the header's, and a name column of 260px after the share indicator, which is 22 characters of a long name against the header's own card's 25.

The same screen, while this playlist is playing

The one state that changes the band rather than the words. The transport is the header's own and it appears in place of the play, which is the header's swap: a card with a play and no steps is a card that cannot skip. At 320px the band has 286.4px of content and the transport is 136px of it, so the three controls sit beside the action row rather than instead of it, and the card is 400.4px in both states.

The playing row in the list is the third fixture, so both readings of "this is what is playing" are on one screen: the pause glyph in the card's band and the equalizer strip on the row's own thumbnail. The card's cover draws no strip, and that is a decision rather than an omission. The strip's bar count solves 7n - 4 against the artwork's content box, which is exact at 96px and 40px and gives 34.57 bars at this cover's 288px, and a comb at that count is a texture rather than an equalizer. Its job is to say which item is playing without a press, and on this screen the row that is playing says it with a shape on its own 40px tile, in the list, where a reader scanning a list looks.

The four states, and the three that compose

Never synced is the empty state, syncing is the header's busy form plus the summary's in-flight figure, and error is the sync error. All three are used as they are and none is redrawn. The fourth, not found, has no component at all and is named at the end of this file.

Never

Never synced, which is lastSyncedAt being null, and it is the empty state in the list area with the card unchanged beside it. The play is disabled rather than absent: a playlist with nothing in it cannot be played, and a control that is there and cannot be pressed is a different thing from a control that is not there. Nothing sits under the card, and that is the case with no figures rather than a summary of no figures: there is no run to summarise and the fault that would own the absence is a different state. The count reads 0 rather than being left out, which is the header's own longer argument and not the shorter comment beside one of its states: trackCount is a stored integer, a stored one is never unknown, and "0 is an answer rather than a placeholder". The header's markup still omits it and that contradiction is the header's to settle, not this screen's. What the mark on the button cost here is nothing, and that was checked rather than assumed. The empty state's Sync now button is 126.81px with the rotate it now carries and 115.8px while one is running, and both sit in a column that is align-items: center, so the width is free: the left column still ends at the same 460.1px it did without the mark. The sync error's button is the same width and sits under the card in a column flex, so that frame's 640.1px is unchanged too.

Syncing

Syncing, which is the header's busy form and the summary's in-flight figure, both used as they are and neither redrawn. The count reads 131 because it is a total of associations and associations arrive during a run; the figures are tabular so the line does not shift as it climbs, which is what the count's own rule says they are for. The summary's kept figure reads 0 and is quiet, because 0 there means "not counted yet" and not "nothing kept", and an accent 0 would be the system announcing its own promise with a number that says it kept none.

Error

Sync failed, which is PlaylistSyncStatus.Error with a run behind it, and the sync error replaces the summary rather than joining it. They are different components with different jobs: the summary says what the run did and the error says what to do about it, so a column carrying both would put the same news in the same 320px twice. The summary's own record forbids the duplication from its side for the same reason. The track list underneath is unchanged, which is the point of the reassurance: a failed sync changed nothing. The button it carries is 126.81px and grew by its mark, rotate-clockwise at --icon-sm, which is the same glyph the overflow menu draws on this same verb at this same access level, so the retry in a panel and the menu item are one control twice. The frame's left column is 640.1px either way: the button is one line in a column flex and its width cannot cost height.

The three access levels, one menu open each

The rule is one sentence, so it can be checked against this screen in one pass: a collaborator may add a track, remove a track and sync, and may not rename, delete or manage shares, and those three stay with the owner. Absent, not disabled. The three owner-only controls are Rename, Delete playlist and share management, and the first two are menu items and the third is the Share item.

access and hasShares are two facts and treating them as one draws the wrong menu for somebody. access is the level that decides the menu; hasShares is a boolean about the playlist rather than the reader. Two menus are drawn open here because one open at a time is the product's behaviour and two open at once would overlap, which is the library's own reason for drawing its levels on three screens.

Owner

Owner: the overflow holds all four items, and the rule before Delete is the header's own. A share indicator, not a collaborator one, because the keys are still yours.

The mobile arrangement, at 390 and 844

One column: the header on top, the rows under it. Nothing is side by side and nothing is shortened to make room for a neighbour, which is the whole difference between the two arrangements: a width on the desk is a division and a width here is the whole frame. Every frame in this section is 390 by 844, the library's own phone rather than a generic one, so two screens claiming numbers about a device are claiming them about the same device. Its content box is 388.4 by 842.4, the frame's border being inside its 390 the way the library's is.

The header is the component's row arrangement, and the measurement is what settled it. The header has two arrangements and at 390 the card is 470.4px and the row is 136px. On 842.4 less a 97px bar that is 275px of list against 609.4px, which is 4 rows against 9 on plain rows, and the card leaves 188.6px once the resting summary and its 20px gap have theirs, so 2. This is the phone's version of the desk's left column, and it is the same discipline: the component's own arrangement at the width, nothing re-decided here.

The header was measured from nothing, which is the gap this arrangement existed to close. [The transport's own record](../../../design-system/components/header-transport.md) measures absolute pixels and never states the width it measured them at: three 48px steps costing 160px of the actions column and leaving the title 750px, one row of five costing 208px and leaving 670px, three equal 48px boxes leaving 718px. Those are 1056px figures and the record did not say so. Its sibling records name both widths. So the phone's header is a fresh measurement and it is reported here: at 388.4 it is 136px tall with the time off the sync line and 136.6px with it on, the cover is 96, the actions column is 72 and the identity block is 180.4px, and 96 + 20 + 180.4 + 20 + 72 = 388.4.

The sync line's time is off, and the arithmetic is exact. The line needs 198.16px: 70.78 for the state, 3.91 for the separator, 99.47 for the time and 12.00 of gap either side of the separator. The identity block has 180.4px, so it is 17.76px short. The component's own answer to that is not to wrap the row, which is flex-wrap: nowrap: it is that the last span wraps inside itself, and measured, that span arrives at 81.71px and takes 32.4px of height instead of 16.2, which makes the header 136.6px and leaves the separator at the end of the line above it, so the line reads Up to date · and then Synced 2 days ago. A middot with nothing after it is not a separator. With the time gone the line is 70.78px on one line, the header is 136, and the separator goes with it. This is the decision the library record already makes at 390 for the same reason, so the two screens agree, and the time is still on the frame as the sync summary's stamp 20px below the header in the resting and syncing states. In the error state the summary is the thing that is gone, and that is the one cost, drawn below.

The header is at the full width, not inset by the page's 16px working inset, and the component's own padding decides it. .hdr declares padding: 20px 0, so it is written to sit at its container's inline edges. Insetting it by 16px would override a rule the header's record owns and would take the drawn name's column from 152.4px to 120px. The name is 204px at --text-xl and truncates either way, so that is 13 characters of it against 10.

No way home, and that is the gesture. The web arrangement carries a chevron and the word Playlists because a browser has no back gesture to fall back on. On mobile the platform returns from a pushed route, so a control that returns is a second way to do what the platform already does, and it is a row the phone would spend 19px of height on for nothing. Its absence here is the gesture rather than an omission.

The bar is the flush arrangement on this frame and the centred one on the desk, which is the player bar's own rule at the two widths rather than a preference: at 390 the centre and the 480px cap are both dropped. The lift takes the centred arrangement as its base and this frame adds the class, so a copy of the bar cannot arrive here carrying the wrong one.

Seven of the fourteen rows clear the bar, and the ticket's eight was an arithmetic figure rather than a measured one. The budget is 842.4 less a 136px header less a 97px bar, which is 609.4px, and eight plain rows of 64.8px is 518.4px of it. But two of the fourteen rows are 76.1px, the failed and unavailable ones, because each carries a reason line 11.3px below the sub line, and 22.6px of extra row is a third of a row. So the list's top is at 222.4px, the bar's top at 745.4px, the eighth row's bottom at 764.2px, and the answer is seven. The shortest viewport that fits this arrangement with nothing scrolled off is 433px, set by the error frame: 136 of header, 20 of gap, 180 of sync error and 97 of bar.

The four states, on the phone

Never

On the phone the same state, and the header's own row arrangement is the reason the empty state has room at all: the card would be 470.4px and this is 136px, so on 842.4 less a 97px bar the difference is 609.4px of list against 275px. The play is disabled for the same reason it is on the desk, and the count reads 0 for the same reason. The time is not on the sync line here, so the line reads Never synced and nothing is lost: the word carries the whole fact on its own. The empty state is 220.4px in 388.4, its reading prose wrapping to two lines and its promise to two, and it is 126.81px wide with the mark it carries on the desk.

Nothing is lost and nothing is repeated. The summary is 90.6px against the resting 66.4px, the 24.2px of difference being its flight line at 16.2 and the gap under it. Its band is four 1fr cells with a --space-3 gap, so at 388.4 each cell is 88.1px against the five-figure figure's 60.01px, which is the desk's 280px floor of 36.04px of slack made irrelevant by the frame being wider than the column was narrow. And the 24.2px costs no row here, which the ticket expected it to: the list starts at 246.6px rather than 222.4 and the eighth row's bottom moves from 764.2px to 788.4px, both of which were already under the 745.4px bar, so the answer is seven rows in both states. The budget is spent by the two 76.1px rows, not by the summary.

Error

On the phone the same state, and it is the one state where dropping the time costs something real, and the one state that costs rows. The desk's sync line read Sync failed · Synced 6 days ago; here it reads Sync failed, and the sync error that replaces the summary carries no stamp of its own, so "Synced 6 days ago" is on no part of this frame. In the resting and syncing states the time is the summary's stamp, which sits directly under the header; in this one the summary is the thing that is gone. That is the whole cost of the decision and it is named rather than discovered later. The error is 180px against the summary's 66.4px, and 113.6px is 1.75 rows, so the list starts at 336px instead of 222.4 and five rows clear the bar instead of seven. Its own button is the same 126.81px with the mark, and it is still one line in a column, so its width costs no height here either.

While this playlist is playing

The header's swap lands differently here, because .actions is a column: the steps go above the shuffle and the overflow rather than beside them, which is the header record's own arrangement for the transport. The actions column is 136px wide while playing against 72px at rest, so the identity block falls from 180.4px to 116.4px and the drawn name's column from 152.4px to 88.4px. That is the binding width on this frame and it is worse than the inset question above: at 88.4px the drawn 204px name shows 7 characters of 17, against 13 at rest. Measured, not assumed, and the reason the header is at the full width is not only the 16px of inset but this.

The way home, and what it costs

A web fact, and the only control on this screen that mobile has no counterpart to. On mobile the platform gesture returns from a pushed route, so a control that returns is a second way to do what the platform already does. Its absence there is the gesture rather than an omission, and the mobile arrangement is drawn below and says so there.

One frame here has no player bar either, and that is the bar's own record rather than this screen's: "a bar that is present but has nothing to play does not exist any more, so the disabled play that this file used to specify for that state is not drawn". A bar carrying a track on a playlist that has never synced would assert playback that the same frame's card says cannot happen, and the two would be one screen's state contradicting itself. The other seven frames carry the bar, which is the point of this being the first screen in the product where it is drawn at rest.

A word and a chevron, and both are load-bearing. The word names the destination, which is what makes the control usable by a screen reader and legible to a reader who has never seen a back chevron; the chevron says which direction, which is what a gallery scanned quickly needs. A word alone reads as a section heading, and a chevron alone is a shape with a name attached to it. The chevron is chevron-left, added to the pin for this one control, one path, verbatim at @tabler/icons 3.48.0, and it takes no optical correction because its ink spans x 9 to x 15 and centres at 12.

It costs one row of fourteen, and the number was nearly reported as zero. The row is 58.9px and the bar's top is at 803.8px. 11 whole rows clear the fold with the way home and 12 do without it, the twelfth row's bottom being at 838.1px with it and 779.2px without, so it is 34.3px under the bar in the first case and whole in the second. The first measurement of that said no change, and the fault had not been applied: taking the row out of the flow and reading the count in the same expression is not the same as reading it after the style is in, and a null result from a fault that never landed is the one number here that would have gone into the record as a fact.

The figures, and the width each came from

the arrangement 1056 x 900 content at 1056 and 900
the left column 320px 40px above the 280px measured floor
the gap 24px --space-6, not the --space-4 two labels want
the track list 712px 1056 less 320 less 24
the cover 288px square 320 less the card's own 16px a side
the name's text column 260px 288 less the indicator's 20 and the 8px gap
characters of a name 22 of a 65-character one, 743px against 260
the meta line 198.16px in 288px the state, a middot and the time
the summary's cells 71px each 60.01px for a five-figure figure
the way home 76.45 x 18.9px in a 58.9px row a chevron and the word Playlists
the scrim 80px, 27.8% of the cover the header's own card is 24.7%
a track row 64.8px 12px of padding, a 40px tile, a 0.8px border
the track list's title 516px 712 less 196px of lanes and gaps
the docked bar 97px 98px in a block, 97 with its border on the edge
rows above the bar 11 of 14 at 900; the twelfth's bottom is 838.1
the left column's height 486.8px, ending at 546.5 the card and the summary beneath it
the bar's top 803.8px 900 less the 97px bar and the 0.8px frame border
the shortest viewport that fits 737.1px set by the fault, the tallest left column
the play, or the transport 48px, or 136px the band is 286.4px in every state

And the phone's, at 390 and 844

A second table rather than more rows in the first, because the record's own warning applies here too: a row in one table headed by 1056 has told the reader the figure is a 1056 figure. Every one of these is a computed box read out of the generated file at 390 wide and 844 tall, and none of them is a figure read off a stylesheet.

the arrangement 390 x 844, content 388.4 x 842.4 the library's own frame
the header 136px the header's row arrangement, unmodified
the cover 96px the header's own cover
the identity block 180.4px 96 + 20 + 180.4 + 20 + 72
the actions column 72px wide, 92px tall 48px play above a 72px row of two
the name's column 152.4px for a 204px name 13 characters of 17
the sync line 70.78px, one line the time is off; 198.16px with it
the header with the time on 136.6px the time arrives at 81.71px and wraps
the identity block, playing 116.4px the actions are 136px wide while playing
the name's column, playing 88.4px 7 characters of 17, the tightest on the screen
the read level's identity block 204.4px the shuffle alone, so 48px of actions
the summary 66.4px, 90.6px in flight four 88.1px cells and the flight line
the sync error 180px against the summary's 66.4px
the empty state 220.4px prose on two lines and its promise on two
the list's top 222.4px 136 + 20 + 66.4
the bar's top 745.4px 842.4 less the 97px bar
rows above the bar 7 of 14 two of the rows are 76.1px, not 64.8
rows above the bar, in error 5 of 14 the error is 113.6px more than the summary
the shortest viewport that fits 433px set by the error frame, as on the desk

Every one of these is a computed box read out of the generated file at 1056 wide and 900 tall, not a figure read off a stylesheet. The 0.8px that appears in the two row heights and in the bar is this environment rendering a 1px border at 0.8, which the playlist header's own record already accounts for.

What composing these cost

Three faults were found by drawing this screen and none was visible from reading the components. Two of them are the same collision seen from two angles, and both are recorded here because the screen found them. The third is a naming problem that is still open.

Every track row in the tree was 120.8px rather than 65px, because the playlist header's .body was landing on the track row's .body. specimen.css declares .body for the header's identity block, and track-row.html declares its own .body inside its own .row without setting display. The header's rule won on the two declarations the row never mentioned, so the row's title and sub line sat inside a 96px min-height flex column instead of a 40px one, and every row measured 120.8px. The 65px that the sync summary, the empty state and this screen all quote was a number no specimen produced. Every legitimate consumer of that rule is a direct child of .hdr and every illegitimate one is a child of .row, so the rule is now .hdr > .body and the rows are 64.8px. Proved behaviour-preserving for the header: all fourteen headers in its own specimen and all nine items on the library measure the same before and after, to the digit.

Every state word in every track row carried a dot it never asked for, and on a phone it cost a whole line. The same collision from a second angle. specimen.css declares .state for the header's sync state, whose ::before is a 7px mark in the state's own tone, and the track row's .state is a single coloured word with no mark and no pseudo-element of its own. So every state word in the row was 15px wider than the word and its 8px gap: measured on the track row's own specimen, "Downloading" was 86.85px and is 71.85px, "Failed" 48.31px and 33.31px. The cost that is worth knowing is on a phone, where the row is narrowest: the failed row's sentence "Download failed, will retry on the next sync" fitted on one line and the dot pushed it onto two, taking the row from 76.1px to 92.3px, which is a whole 16.2px line and a quarter of a row. The rule is now scoped to .hdr .state and .mhdr .state, proved behaviour-preserving the same way: all nineteen of the header's own states and all twenty of the library's keep the 7px mark, and all fourteen header figures and all nine library items are unchanged to the digit. The row's own 3px .dot span, the one it does ask for, is unaffected, because it is a span and not a state.

Five of the track row's class names are also specimen.css's, so the row's rules have to be namespaced to be composed beside the header. row, play, state, lane and art are declared in both files, and on a screen that draws the header and the track row at once all five are on the page. .play is the one that cannot be worked around: the header's is 48px and the row's is 28px, and the morph's block addresses the name unprefixed, so a screen that drew both unprefixed would have one of them win on source order with nothing to say which. The rules are therefore lifted and namespaced under .tl by the generator, which is a descendant combinator and so raises every lifted rule's specificity by one class. The markup is not renamed, so the morph's host list is untouched and stays at four. The durable fix is a second shared block with distinct names, which is a change to the track row and belongs to a ticket about the track row.

Every claim on this screen was proved by putting the fault back, and the numbers are what each one showed. The namespacing removed: the row's play goes 28px to 48px, the row 64.8px to 72.8px and the fold 11 rows to 10. The left column at 280px: the band holds and the cover drops to 248px, which is the whole cost of the 40px of slack. The column at 276px: each band cell is 60px and a five-figure kept count is 60.01px, so it does not fit by a hundredth of a pixel. The way home taken out of the flow: the first row's bottom moves from 125.3px to 66.4px and the fold 11 to 12. The anchors left unstyled: the name's colour becomes the user agent's rgb(158, 158, 255) and its underline comes back, which no check in the tree can see because neither is a literal in a file. The gap at --space-4: the track list is 720px rather than 712px and nothing breaks, which is why that one is written above as an argument and not as a finding.

One of those six was nearly recorded as the opposite of what it showed. The first measurement of the way home said the fold did not change, and the fault had not been applied: the style was appended and the count was read in the same expression, and a null result from a fault that never landed is indistinguishable from a null result that did. It was caught by re-measuring with the injected rule's own computed display asserted in the same call, and the difference is one row. The rule that came out of it is the one this record has used all along: assert the fault is applied before believing the number it produced.

Neither is the sync summary's problem, and that is measured. Its class names are local to its own file, so it needed no namespacing, and its four cells fit a 320px column with room: 71px a cell against 60.01px for a five-figure kept count and 47.4px for the widest of the four words, which is "removed". The band sits on --bg rather than on a --surface panel, which its own record hands to the screen: every pairing holds either way, and a panel here would buy nothing over a left column that already has a surface.

Not drawn in this pass

Three things the ticket asks for, named here with what each of them still needs so that nothing is quietly missing from a file that claims to be the screen. The mobile arrangement was the fourth and is now drawn above.

The gap the mobile pass closed, and what it cost to close it. The arrangement could not be assumed from the web one because the transport's own record measures absolute pixels and never states the width it measured them at, so the phone's header had to be measured from nothing rather than scaled. That record's numbers are now attributed in place. What the pass found that a scale would have hidden: the header's row arrangement, not its card, is the one that fits, because they are 136px and 470.4px at 390 and the gap is nine rows against four; the sync line is 17.76px short of its own three spans and wraps its time inside itself rather than its row, so the time comes off; the actions column is 136px wide while playing against 72px at rest, which is the tightest width anywhere on the screen at 88.4px; and the height budget is spent by two 76.1px rows rather than by any of the components above them, which is why the ticket's eight rows is seven.

The not-found state. It has no component, and it needs one: its own record and its own specimen. The empty state cannot stand in for it, because the empty state's words say that nothing is here because the playlist has never synced, which is a lie for a playlist that was shared to this account and is not any more. A playlist that does not exist and a playlist the account cannot see both answer 404 at one status, so the state has to speak about both without claiming to know which happened.

The share dialog and the add-a-video dialog. Both are hosted here and nowhere else, on both arrangements. The second is on the detail only, with this playlist preselected and any other writable playlist selectable, and it issues one POST /playlists/:id/tracks per chosen playlist because no multi-playlist route exists, which is a fact the checklist has to say out loud rather than imply. Both need their own records, and a dialog is narrower on one arrangement than on the other, so neither can be drawn once.

A queue. Deliberately not drawn, and not a gap: it is a panel on the player bar's record and it can be opened from here on either arrangement. This screen places no control for it, which is the correct answer rather than an omission.

Usage

Do keep the two columns and the gap, and do keep the left column at 320px: the band's five-figure case needs 276.04px and the round number above it is what gives the track list 712px. Do draw the count at zero on a playlist that has never synced, because a stored integer of zero is an answer. Do gate the three owner-only controls by absence rather than by disabling them. Do keep the sync error and the sync summary out of the same column. Do not draw a way-home control on the mobile arrangement. Do not namespace a component's rules by renaming its classes when a scope on the lifted rules settles the collision, because the morph's block addresses three of those names unprefixed.
